mission: PauseAI is a grassroots movement that wants a global, treaty-based pause on training the most powerful general AI systems until they can be built safely and kept under democratic control. Volunteers hold protests (starting outside Microsoft's Brussels office in 2023 and at every AI summit since), lobby lawmakers and run public campaigns; PauseAI US organises local groups and congressional meetings across the United States.

key_work.title: PauseAI Proposal (global pause treaty)
key_work.plain_summary: Calls for an international treaty creating an IAEA-style 'AI Safety Agency' that must approve big training runs, verified through chip tracking, data-centre inspections and whistleblower incentives.

key_work.title: Statement on Superintelligence (campaign support)
key_work.plain_summary: PauseAI promotes the call to prohibit superintelligence until there is broad scientific consensus it can be done safely and strong public buy-in (110,000+ signatories, per its homepage).

key_work.title: PauseAI US: History and campaigns
key_work.plain_summary: PauseAI US describes its first protests at OpenAI and Meta (2023), national local groups (2024) and its part in defeating a proposed federal ban on state AI laws, struck down 99–1 in the Senate (2025).

key_work.title: PauseAI Roadmap and Funding Scenarios
key_work.plain_summary: Explains PauseAI Global's federation structure, small paid team and theory of change: turning public concern into organised political pressure.

warnings.text: Racing to build ever more powerful AI risks human extinction.
We might build superhuman AI very soon, before we know how to control it.
AI labs are racing to automate every job; job loss is 'only the tip of the iceberg'.
Companies will not pause alone because of competition, so voluntary restraint is not enough.

recommendations.text: Pause training of the most powerful general AI systems via an international treaty involving both the US and China.
Create an international AI Safety Agency to approve major training runs and deployments.
Use the concentrated chip supply chain (e.g. tracking GPUs, inspecting fabs and data centres) to verify compliance.
Citizens should contact representatives, join local groups and protest peacefully.
